1: # Minimal translation from accepted NL0
2: 
3: Start with the accepted source map and specification. Read the supplied proof
4: and definitions where needed to choose faithful types. Other Yui documents,
5: library searches and individual background notes are available on demand;
6: there is no requirement to preload the entire skill or all note bodies.
7: 
8: 1. Preserve the accepted source and Audit A. Use a source revision only when an
9:    actual mathematical change or useful shared extraction requires it. Reusing
10:    unchanged acceptance runs integrity checks, not another model Audit A.
11: 2. Choose the mathematical representation, complete original H/E input types,
12:    N/P output types and useful local proof obligations. The controller copies
13:    source paragraphs and note locations. Mathlib is freely available; retain an
14:    M port only when useful, otherwise apply the library directly. Supply short
15:    `endpoint_correspondence` notes for every E and complete P (including all
16:    hypotheses), explaining direct or equivalent translation. Save partial interface drafts, revise
17:    those drafts, and use small Lean probes for uncertain types. Do not restart
18:    from an empty interface after an ordinary error.
19: 3. Type-check source correspondence, dependency boundaries and the complete
20:    interface, then obtain a separate independent semantic interface review.
21:    Normal full/translation entry dispatches no proof worker before its actual
22:    hash-bound receipt passes. Repair located failures with the interface author
23:    and have the same separate reviewer assess changed output. Final machine Audit B
24:    inherits that review only if the actual complete artifact preserves the freeze. The
25:    lower-level legacy mechanical freeze can record `PENDING_AUDIT_B`; it does
26:    not satisfy this normal-workflow pre-proof gate.
27: 4. Run local proof workers on frozen conditional obligations. Each gets its
28:    input statements, matched source paragraphs and own compact note index.
29:    Read a full note only if useful. No sibling proof bodies, other cases,
30:    developer history or additional personal skills are supplied.
31:    Use [Lean implementation safeguards](lean-writing.md) for library
32:    applications and conversions, including small type checks in preparation.
33:    Yui proof workers receive these requirements in their stage instructions.
34: 5. Attempt mechanical [assembly](assembly.md) and complete native inspection.
35:    Use the serial connection author only for real connection/library-discharge
36:    repair under unchanged E/P/definitions. Normal final Audit B is machine-only:
37:    inherit the actual pre-proof semantics after checking full endpoint types,
38:    defining header and complete closure. Only proof-valid interface drift opens
39:    B-final. Faithful drift is warning-qualified; a nonpass waits for the user's
40:    explicit delivery/recheck/translation-reset choice. Invalid proof is never
41:    semantically overridden.
42: 
43: ## Background notes are references, not extra ports
44: 
45: New contracts select `source.background_mode: node_local_reference`. Original
46: H/E/M/N/P entries remain unchanged; Audit A's verified supplement remains
47: hash-bound. Do not turn every note into a new M root, retype its entire library
48: signature, or require an extra theorem merely to restate it. The frozen
49: stage-one text's historical `background.effective` expansion is still supported
50: as `promoted_inputs` for old contracts; it is not the new translation default.
51: 
52: At the pre-freeze semantic review and final Audit B, notes are guidance, not library permissions. All proved results in
53: the pinned Mathlib environment are available without registration. Review every
54: external E and complete P against its actual Lean type using the concise author
55: correspondence explanation; independently check direct or equivalent meaning.
56: A new external assumption or stronger hypothesis still returns to the source
57: boundary. See [the complete Audit B standard](audit-b.md).
58: 
59: ## Work continuously, report genuine blockers
60: 
61: There is no ordinary `TASK_INCOMPLETE` reporting tool. While unfinished, keep
62: making concrete edits, queries or proof checks. Submit a completed artifact or
63: report a supported mathematical/source/input blocker. If a model turn ends
64: without either, the controller sends one short continuation instruction; it
65: does not demand a progress essay. State/usage recording is programmatic.
66: Proof workers follow [structured diagnosis and repair](proof-repair.md): report
67: actual packet obstructions. Progress counters are passive; no idle-turn count
68: cancels sibling work or authorizes interface changes.
69: 
70: Whole-case/stage execution, total tokens and calls are unlimited by default.
71: Each native check has the configured 300-second wall limit and finite Lean
72: heartbeat policy. Keep measuring usage and allow explicit
73: cancellation. Only a user-requested finite case deadline covers the entire
74: translation, including preparation, queue waiting, parallel proofs, assembly
75: and Audit B; later stages cannot reset that optional deadline. Preserve partial
76: results and report execution health separately from mathematical acceptance.

value.representation_notes: Use the actual complex Lie algebra LR.L=LieAlgebra.SpecialLinear.sl (Fin 2) ℂ, the subtype of trace-zero 2×2 matrices with commutator bracket (pinned Classical.lean:94–99). x,y,h remain arbitrary Chevalley generators: H002 explicitly records IsSl2Triple h x y, their complex linear span being all of LR.L, the Lie representation law, finite dimension λ+1, irreducibility and existence of a primitive highest-weight vector. The pinned IsSl2Triple declaration includes h≠0 and exactly [x,y]=h, [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=−2y, where 2• is natural repeated addition. A linear rho plus its explicit H002 commutator law is the usual Lie representation, avoiding an implicit theorem in a typeclass. H003 retains the chosen nonzero highest-weight vector. H001 keeps primality, CharP, nonnegativity and the strict λ

steps.statement: LR.Strings l (rho x) (rho y) (rho h) v
steps.explanation: Unpack the representation and Chevalley commutator laws; induct simultaneously on the natural exponent. H001 identifies nonnegative integer exponents with naturals.

steps.statement: (∀ i : LR.I l, LR.eNat (rho y) v i.val ≠ 0) ∧ LinearIndependent ℂ (fun i : LR.I l => LR.eNat (rho y) v i.val)
steps.explanation: Apply repeated raising to prove nonvanishing. Isolate each coefficient by the product of h minus the other complex weights; cancel the nonzero weight differences. Do not use distinctness in characteristic p.

steps.statement: LR.BasisString l (rho y) v
steps.explanation: Use the independent family of size finrank to construct the basis. Expand the next lowering vector, compare its weight with every basis weight, and deduce termination and all higher vanishings.

steps.statement: LR.Matrices l (rho x) (rho y) (rho h) (LR.eNat (rho y) v)
steps.explanation: Divide the string formulas by complex factorials, retaining the endpoint zero cases.

steps.statement: LR.N1 l (rho x) (rho y) (rho h) v
steps.explanation: Iterate the matrices to derive both divided-power formulas and zero cases, using Nat.choose and its factorial identity under the displayed natural bounds. Assemble N001 including the basis, strings, termination, cardinality and integer coefficients.

steps.statement: LR.LocalRingSpec p ∧ ∃ (m : Module.Basis (LR.I l) ℤ M) (bc : Module.Basis (LR.I l) ℂ V), ∀ i, (m i : V) = bc i
steps.explanation: Prove that the explicit fraction set is a subring, so its closure is exactly itself, and prove the unit criterion. Reindex a simultaneous lattice/complex basis by I using finite-dimensionality and cardinality; use the library's strong rank condition for the field.

steps.statement: Nonempty (LR.Action K M rho x y h) ∧ ∃ f : LR.MR p M →ₗ[ℤ] V, LR.IotaSpec p M f ∧ LR.LocalBasis p l M f ∧ LR.Preserved p M f (rho x) (rho y)
steps.explanation: Base-change the simultaneous integer basis to R; construct the pure-tensor embedding and prove injectivity through complex independence. Extend lattice operators to the scalar extension, prove bracket closure of the integer span, and construct the induced K-linear action with its pure-tensor commutator law.

steps.statement: LR.SmallUnits p l
steps.explanation: Apply the pinned factorial divisibility theorem at r≤l.toNat<p. Use the exact R fraction characterization to invert factorials and each binomial coefficient.

steps.statement: ∀ b : Module.Basis (LR.I l) ℂ V, LR.BasisSpec l (rho y) v b → LR.UnitIdentities l (rho x) (rho y) b
steps.explanation: Check the three operator identities on every basis vector using the existing divided-power formulas; Fin.last l.toNat represents the source index λ.

steps.statement: LR.N2 p l K M rho x y h v
steps.explanation: Combine the three identities and invert the binomial scalar to obtain each matrix unit. Closure under composition and R-scalars proves preservation of the embedded arbitrary lattice. Bundle all N002 clauses without assuming an embedding or action in advance.

steps.statement: ∀ (r : LR.R p) (c : LR.C p), LR.cv p (r • c) = (((r : ℚ) : ℂ)) * LR.cv p c
steps.explanation: Checked representation bridge for the restriction-of-scalars wrapper: use the pinned RestrictScalars.smul_def and the subtype algebra map R→ℚ followed by the rational embedding ℚ→ℂ. cv is the supplied additive equivalence, so zero, sums and bijectivity already hold.

steps.statement: ∀ f : LR.MR p M →ₗ[ℤ] V, LR.IotaSpec p M f → ∃ J : Submodule (LR.R p) (LR.C p), LR.CoeffSpec p l (rho y) v M f J
steps.explanation: The pure-tensor specification makes f the unique canonical embedding. Matrix units identify all coordinate modules with J0; projected finite basis coordinates generate J. Prove it nonzero and build the coordinate R-linear equivalence. cv makes the restriction-of-scalars identification explicit.

steps.statement: ∀ J : Submodule (LR.R p) (LR.C p), J.FG → LR.RationalEmbedding p J
steps.explanation: Tensor a finite generating set to prove finite-dimensionality. Construct μ by multiplication; put any finite tensor sum over a common nonzero integer denominator to prove injectivity. Its range is exactly the rational span.

steps.statement: Module.finrank ℚ (ℚ ⊗[LR.R p] LR.MR p M) = l.toNat+1
steps.explanation: Choose the R-basis exported by N002 and apply Basis.baseChange over ℚ, then finrank_eq_card_basis. No M premise port is required.

steps.statement: ∀ (f : LR.MR p M →ₗ[ℤ] V) (J : Submodule (LR.R p) (LR.C p)), LR.IotaSpec p M f → LR.CoeffSpec p l (rho y) v M f J → Module.finrank ℚ (ℚ ⊗[LR.R p] J) = 1
steps.explanation: Tensor the coordinate equivalence with ℚ. Construct inverse coordinate maps to identify the result with I→(ℚ⊗R J). Use finite-dimensional product finrank to get n=n*r and cancel positive n.

steps.statement: ∀ J : Submodule (LR.R p) (LR.C p), LR.RationalEmbedding p J → Module.finrank ℚ (ℚ ⊗[LR.R p] J) = 1 → LR.RationalMultiples p J
steps.explanation: For any chosen nonzero a∈J, μ shows 1⊗a is nonzero. Its independent singleton spans the one-dimensional rational tensor space, so applying μ writes every element of J as a rational multiple of a.

steps.statement: LR.PDecomposition p
steps.explanation: Factor the nonzero integer numerator and positive denominator by powers of p. The remaining signed fraction and its inverse lie in R; package it as a unit. The integer exponent uses field zpow, allowing negative valuations.

steps.statement: LR.N3 p l (rho y) v M
steps.explanation: Use a finite nonempty list of nonzero generators, rational multiples of a and their p-decompositions. A minimum valuation produces b and J=Rb. Prove the scaled basis property for every such nonzero generator; bundle the coordinate decomposition, μ and rational rank as N003.

steps.statement: Nonempty (LR.Residue p K)
steps.explanation: Construct the maps R→K and R→ZMod p by the fraction formula; prove compatibility with the prime-field map, surjectivity, kernel pR and the quotient ring equivalence, and that units have nonzero images.

steps.statement: ∀ Q : LR.Residue p K, LR.Bridge p K M Q
steps.explanation: Construct Γ and Δ with their specified inverses by tensor/quotient universal properties. ModN is the actual quotient by p multiples with its canonical ZMod action. Check formulas on pure tensors and prove commutation with arbitrary induced lattice and R-linear operators.

steps.statement: ∀ Q : LR.Residue p K, LR.Transfer p l K M (rho y) v Q
steps.explanation: For every specified scaled R-basis, base-change to K and transport through Γ. The first-factor convention incorporates the source tensor flips. Preserve the chosen b and basis vectors, and prove the stated K-dimension.

steps.statement: ∀ Q : LR.Residue p K, LR.MatrixTransport p l K M rho x y h v Q
steps.explanation: For any witnesses satisfying the exact embedding and Γ formulas, transport integer action matrices and all divided-power matrices. The integer coefficients commute with the ring maps; injectivity of f identifies the required lattice vectors. Construct the reduced operators from actual restrictions.

steps.statement: LR.SmallPowers l K M rho x y h
steps.explanation: Tensor the characteristic-zero identities r!X(r)=x^r and r!Y(r)=y^r. Their restrictions exist by N002; the residue/unit facts make r! nonzero for r≤λ, so cancellation yields the two reduced divided powers.

steps.statement: ∀ Q : LR.Residue p K, LR.PolynomialTransport p l K M rho x y h v Q
steps.explanation: Extend the already proved localized matrix-unit identity through Γ, using equality on pure tensors and preservation of compositions. Substitute the small divided-power equalities to obtain the exact polynomial and its coordinate action. All indices λ−i, λ, λ−j satisfy the small-power guard.

steps.statement: LR.N4 p l K M rho x y h v
steps.explanation: Assemble N004: choose residue data, canonical f, coefficient module J and a nonzero cyclic generator from N003, then a scaled R-basis and its transported K-basis. Keep these same witnesses for all matrices and formulas. Export both tensor identifications, the positive dimension, and every reduced matrix-unit clause.

steps.statement: ∀ (A : LR.Action K M rho x y h) (W : Submodule K (LR.VK K M)), LR.Stable W A.a → LR.Stable W A.d → ∀ i j : LR.I l, LR.Stable W (LR.polynomial l A.a A.d i j)
steps.explanation: Finite induction proves that invariant subspaces are stable under all nonnegative powers, their compositions and K-scalar multiples. Apply this to the displayed polynomial.

steps.statement: ∀ (beta : Module.Basis (LR.I l) K (LR.VK K M)) (W : Submodule K (LR.VK K M)), W ≠ ⊥ → ∃ (w : LR.VK K M) (c : LR.I l → K) (j : LR.I l), w ∈ W ∧ w ≠ 0 ∧ w = ∑ i, c i • beta i ∧ c j ≠ 0
steps.explanation: Choose a nonzero vector of the nonzero subspace, expand it in the finite basis and select a nonzero coefficient. Close all witnesses inside the existential statement.

steps.statement: ∀ (A : LR.Action K M rho x y h) (beta : Module.Basis (LR.I l) K (LR.VK K M)) (W : Submodule K (LR.VK K M)), (∀ i j k : LR.I l, LR.polynomial l A.a A.d i j (beta k) = if k = j then beta i else 0) → (∀ i j : LR.I l, LR.Stable W (LR.polynomial l A.a A.d i j)) → W ≠ ⊥ → W = ⊤
steps.explanation: Use the same w,c,j witnesses. Each matrix unit sends w to c_j beta_i; cancel the nonzero scalar in K, then use spanning of the basis.

steps.statement: LR.Target K M rho x y h
steps.explanation: Choose the induced action from N002 and the basis exported by N004. Its positive cardinality proves nontriviality. For every invariant subspace use the zero case or T028. The integer span's scalar extension has the same invariant subspaces as its three generators; no reduced weight separation or algebraic closure is used.

value.full_target:
Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.
value.conclusion: V_K is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W⊂V_K invariant under ρ_K(x⊗1), ρ_K(y⊗1), and ρ_K(h⊗1), either W={0} or W=V_K. Thus V(K) is irreducible as an L(K)-module, for every field K and every prime p and integer 0≤λ<p, including λ=0 and p=2.

hypotheses.statement: p is prime, K has characteristic p, and λ is an integer with 0≤λ<p.

V=V(λ) is the complex irreducible highest-weight sl₂(ℂ)-module of highest weight λ, has complex dimension λ+1, and its Chevalley generators x,y,h satisfy [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=−2y, [x,y]=h, both in sl₂(ℂ) and in their actions on V.
v∈V is nonzero, xv=0 and hv=λv.

M⊂V is an admissible lattice: it is a free abelian subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis of V, and it is stable under U_Z. The lattice is arbitrary; it is not assumed to be the minimal lattice.

definitions.definition: I={i∈ℤ:0≤i≤λ}; indices of finite sums and indexed families in this proof range over I unless another range is displayed.

definitions.type: family of elements of U(sl₂(ℂ)) and their induced operators on V, indexed by nonnegative integers
definitions.definition: For every integer r≥0, X(r)=X_r=x^r/r! in the complex universal enveloping algebra U(sl₂(ℂ)); the same notation denotes its action on V. Powers are compositions on V, with zeroth power the identity.

definitions.type: family of elements of U(sl₂(ℂ)) and their induced operators on V, indexed by nonnegative integers
definitions.definition: For every integer r≥0, Y(r)=Y_r=y^r/r! in U(sl₂(ℂ)); the same notation denotes its action on V, with zeroth power the identity.
U_Z is the unital ℤ-subalgebra of U(sl₂(ℂ)) generated by X(r) and Y(r) for all integers r≥0, acting on V by its given sl₂(ℂ)-representation.

definitions.type: p-local subring of ℚ, with its usual inclusion in ℂ
definitions.definition: R=ℤ_(p)={a/b∈ℚ:a,b∈ℤ, b≠0, p∤b}, with the operations inherited from ℚ and its usual embedding in ℂ.
M_R=R⊗_ℤ M. Its elementary tensors are written r⊗m with r∈R and m∈M.
ι_M(r⊗m)=r m, extending by addition from pure tensors, where R⊂ℂ and M⊂V. When its injectivity has been proved we identify M_R with its image under ι_M.
For i,j∈I, E_ij=E(i,j) is the unique complex-linear operator sending e_j to e_i and e_k to zero for each k∈I with k≠j.
Π=Y(λ)X(λ), with rightmost factor applied first.

definitions.type: family of R-submodules of ℂ indexed by I
definitions.definition: For i∈I, J_i={c∈ℂ:c e_i∈ι_M(M_R)}. Scalar operations are inherited from ℂ.
V_K=V(K)=M⊗_ℤ K, with K acting on the second tensor factor.

definitions.type: K-vector space obtained from the Chevalley integer form
definitions.definition: L_K=L(K)=(ℤx+ℤy+ℤh)⊗_ℤ K. The integer span uses the Chevalley generators in sl₂(ℂ) and its inherited bracket, and scalar extension gives the bracket on L_K.
For t∈ℤx+ℤy+ℤh, c,d∈K and m∈M, ρ_K(t⊗c)(m⊗d)=(tm)⊗(cd), extended additively and K-linearly. On V_K the words invariant under x,y,h mean invariant under ρ_K(x⊗1), ρ_K(y⊗1), ρ_K(h⊗1).
F_p=ℤ/pℤ, with residue classes of integers and quotient ring operations; its canonical map into K is [a]↦a·1_K.

result.text:
1: # Irreducibility after reduction of an admissible sl2 lattice
2: 
3: ## Original exercise
4: 
5: James E. Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*,
6: Graduate Texts in Mathematics 9, Springer, section 27, exercise 7,
7: printed page 164. The exercise-list convention on page 163 sets
8: \(L=\mathfrak{sl}_2\) and identifies weights with integers.
9: Book DOI: [10.1007/978-1-4612-6398-2](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4612-6398-2).
10: 
11: > 7. If \(0\leq\lambda<\operatorname{char}K\), \(V=V(\lambda)\),
12: > prove that \(V(K)\) is irreducible as \(L(K)\)-module.
13: 
14: ## Definitions and complete target
15: 
16: Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
17: \(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
18: Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
19: \(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
20: of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy
21: 
22: \[
23: [h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
24: \]
25: 
26: Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
27: \(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
28: the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
29: \(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
30: An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
31: subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
32: \(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.
33: 
34: Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
35: \(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
36: acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
37: \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
38: Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
39: invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
40: Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
41: algebraically closed.
42: 
43: ## Fixed natural-language proof
44: 
45: ### 1. Divided-power coordinates in characteristic zero
46: 
47: Put \(n=\lambda+1\) and \(e_i=y^iv/i!\) for \(0\leq i\leq\lambda\).
48: The commutator identities give, by induction,
49: 
50: \[
51: hy^iv=(\lambda-2i)y^iv,\qquad
52: xy^iv=i(\lambda-i+1)y^{i-1}v\quad(i\geq1).
53: \]
54: 
55: For \(i\leq\lambda\), applying \(x^i\) to \(y^iv\) gives
56: \(i!\lambda(\lambda-1)\cdots(\lambda-i+1)v\ne0\) over \(\mathbb C\).
57: At \(i=0\) the empty product is one. Thus every \(e_i\ne0\).
58: Their \(h\)-eigenvalues \(\lambda-2i\) are distinct over \(\mathbb C\),
59: so they are linearly independent: applying
60: \(\prod_{k\ne j}(h-(\lambda-2k)\mathrm{Id})\) to a relation isolates
61: its \(j\)-th coefficient with a nonzero multiplier.
62: There are \(n\) vectors, the dimension of \(V(\lambda)\), hence they
63: form a basis. Also \(y^{\lambda+1}v=0\), since otherwise it would be
64: an eigenvector of eigenvalue \(-\lambda-2\), absent from this basis.
65: All higher lowering powers vanish as well.
66: 
67: The operator matrices are therefore
68: 
69: \[
70: xe_0=0,\quad xe_i=(\lambda-i+1)e_{i-1}\ (i\geq1),\qquad
71: ye_i=(i+1)e_{i+1}\ (i<\lambda),\quad ye_\lambda=0,
72: \quad he_i=(\lambda-2i)e_i.
73: \]
74: 
75: Iteration gives the integral divided-power matrices
76: 
77: \[
78: X_re_i=\binom{\lambda-i+r}{r}e_{i-r}\quad(0\leq r\leq i),
79: \qquad
80: Y_re_i=\binom{i+r}{r}e_{i+r}\quad(i+r\leq\lambda).       \tag{1}
81: \]
82: 
83: The respective expressions are zero when \(r>i\) or
84: \(i+r>\lambda\), by termination of the strings just proved.
85: 
86: ### 2. Matrix units preserve the localized arbitrary lattice
87: 
88: Let \(R=\mathbb Z_{(p)}=\{a/b\in\mathbb Q:p\nmid b\}\), and regard
89: \(M_R=R\otimes_{\mathbb Z}M\) as a submodule of \(V(\lambda)\).
90: The embedding is injective because an integer basis of \(M\) is
91: complex-linearly independent. The module \(M_R\) is free of rank \(n\)
92: over \(R\) and is preserved by all \(X_r,Y_r\), by admissibility.
93: 
94: Define \(E_{ij}\) to send \(e_j\) to \(e_i\) and all other basis
95: vectors to zero. Formula (1) gives
96: 
97: \[
98: P:=Y_\lambda X_\lambda=E_{\lambda\lambda},\qquad
99: X_{\lambda-i}P=E_{i\lambda},\qquad
100: P Y_{\lambda-j}=\binom\lambda j E_{\lambda j}.
101: \]
102: 
103: For the last identity, an input index below \(j\) is sent below
104: \(e_\lambda\) and killed by \(P\); an index above \(j\) is sent past
105: the end of the lowering string. On \(e_j\) the coefficient is precisely
106: \(\binom\lambda j\). Since \(\lambda<p\), none of
107: \(\lambda!\), \(j!\), \((\lambda-j)!\) is divisible by \(p\), so
108: \(\binom\lambda j\) is a unit in \(R\). Consequently
109: 
110: \[
111: E_{ij}=\left(\binom\lambda j\right)^{-1}
112:        X_{\lambda-i}P Y_{\lambda-j}.                 \tag{2}
113: \]
114: 
115: Every matrix unit preserves \(M_R\). No assertion about distinct
116: weights modulo \(p\) has been used.
117: 
118: ### 3. Recover a standard basis for the arbitrary lattice
119: 
120: Define \(J_i=\{c\in\mathbb C:c e_i\in M_R\}\).
121: The coordinate projection \(E_{ii}\) maps \(M_R\) onto \(J_i e_i\).
122: Applying \(E_{ij}\) to \(c e_j\) shows \(J_j\subseteq J_i\);
123: reversing the indices gives equality. Let \(J\) be their common module.
124: It is finitely generated, being a projection of a finite free module,
125: and nonzero because \(M_R\) spans \(V(\lambda)\) over \(\mathbb C\).
126: The coordinate projections and independence of the \(e_i\) give
127: 
128: \[
129: M_R=\bigoplus_{i=0}^{\lambda}J e_i.                  \tag{3}
130: \]
131: 
132: One must still prove that \(J\) has rank one; containment in
133: \(\mathbb C\) alone does not imply that. Let
134: \(r=\dim_{\mathbb Q}(\mathbb Q\otimes_R J)\), which is finite.
135: Tensoring (3) with the fraction field \(\mathbb Q\) and using the
136: rank \(n\) of \(M_R\) gives \(n=nr\), so \(r=1\), since \(n>0\).
137: The multiplication map \(\mathbb Q\otimes_R J\to\mathbb C\) is
138: injective: this tensor product is the localization of the torsion-free
139: module \(J\subset\mathbb C\), and a fraction mapping to zero has
140: zero numerator. Thus \(J\) spans a one-dimensional rational line.
141: 
142: Choose \(0\ne a\in J\) and write a finite set of nonzero generators
143: as \(q_1a,\ldots,q_ka\) with \(q_j\in\mathbb Q^\times\).
144: Each \(q_j=p^{\nu_j}u_j\) for \(\nu_j\in\mathbb Z\) and a unit
145: \(u_j\) of \(R\). Let \(\nu=\min_j\nu_j\). All generators belong
146: to \(p^\nu R a\), and a generator with minimal exponent generates
147: that whole module. Therefore \(J=Rb\) for a nonzero \(b\in J\).
148: By (3), \(b e_0,\ldots,b e_\lambda\) is an \(R\)-basis of \(M_R\).
149: 
150: ### 4. Reduce and extend scalars
151: 
152: All denominators in \(R\) are invertible in \(K\), so the integer map
153: extends to \(R\to K\). The natural tensor maps give
154: 
155: \[
156: M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\cong M_R\otimes_R K
157: \cong(M_R/pM_R)\otimes_{\mathbb F_p}K.
158: \]
159: 
160: For example the first map sends \(m\otimes c\) to
161: \((1\otimes m)\otimes c\); its inverse sends
162: \((r\otimes m)\otimes c\) to \(m\otimes\bar r c\).
163: The reduced images \(b_0,\ldots,b_\lambda\) of \(b e_i\) form a
164: \(K\)-basis, with exactly the matrices of step 1 reduced into \(K\).
165: The matrix-unit identities (2) persist on this basis.
166: 
167: For \(0\leq r\leq\lambda<p\), \(r!\ne0\) in \(K\), and the induced
168: \(X_r,Y_r\) equal \((r!)^{-1}x^r,(r!)^{-1}y^r\). Hence any
169: \(K\)-subspace invariant under \(x,y\) is invariant under every matrix
170: unit in (2).
171: 
172: ### 5. Conclude irreducibility
173: 
174: Let \(W\) be invariant. If it is nonzero, choose
175: \(0\ne w=\sum_i c_i b_i\in W\), and an index \(j\) with \(c_j\ne0\).
176: For every \(i\), \(E_{ij}w=c_jb_i\in W\). Division by \(c_j\)
177: gives \(b_i\in W\), so all basis vectors lie in \(W\) and
178: \(W=V(K)\). Since \(\dim_K V(K)=\lambda+1>0\), it is nonzero and
179: irreducible. If \(\lambda=0\), all relevant factorials and binomial
180: coefficients are one and the argument applies unchanged. For \(p=2\),
181: the allowed \(\lambda\) are zero and one; the proof still works
182: without requiring distinct reduced \(h\)-eigenvalues.

188: def ReducedBasisSpec (l : ℤ) (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V)
189:     (rho : L →ₗ[ℂ] Module.End ℂ V) (x y h : L) (A : Action K M rho x y h)
190:     (beta : Module.Basis (I l) K (VK K M)) : Prop :=
191:   Module.finrank K (VK K M) = l.toNat+1 ∧
192:   Matrices l A.a A.d A.t (extend l beta) ∧
193:   (∀ r : ℕ, r ≤ l.toNat →
194:     (r.factorial : K) ≠ 0 ∧
195:     Lift K M (dp (rho x) r) (((r.factorial : K)⁻¹) • A.a^r) ∧
196:     Lift K M (dp (rho y) r) (((r.factorial : K)⁻¹) • A.d^r)) ∧
197:   (∀ i j : I l, (Nat.choose l.toNat j.val : K) ≠ 0 ∧
198:     ∀ k : I l, polynomial l A.a A.d i j (beta k) = if k = j then beta i else 0)
199: def Transfer (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V)
200:     (d : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (Q : Residue p K) : Prop :=
201:   letI := Q.phi.toAlgebra
202:   ∀ (f : MR p M →ₗ[ℤ] V) (b : ℂ), IotaSpec p M f → ScaledBasis p l d v M f b →
203:     ∃ (G : VK K M ≃ₗ[K] K ⊗[R p] MR p M)
204:       (B : Module.Basis (I l) (R p) (MR p M)) (beta : Module.Basis (I l) K (VK K M)),
205:       GammaPure p K M Q.phi G ∧
206:       (∀ i, f (B i) = b • eNat d v i.val) ∧
207:       (∀ i, beta i = G.symm (1 ⊗ₜ[R p] B i)) ∧
208:       Module.finrank K (VK K M) = l.toNat+1
209: def ReducedPackage (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V)
210:     (rho : L →ₗ[ℂ] Module.End ℂ V) (x y h : L) (v : V) (Q : Residue p K) : Prop :=
211:   letI := Q.phi.toAlgebra
212:   ∀ A : Action K M rho x y h,
213:     ∃ (f : MR p M →ₗ[ℤ] V) (J : Submodule (R p) (C p)) (b : ℂ)
214:       (G : VK K M ≃ₗ[K] K ⊗[R p] MR p M)
215:       (B : Module.Basis (I l) (R p) (MR p M)) (beta : Module.Basis (I l) K (VK K M)),
216:       IotaSpec p M f ∧ Function.Injective f ∧ CoeffSpec p l (rho y) v M f J ∧
217:       (cv p).symm b ∈ J ∧ b ≠ 0 ∧ J = Submodule.span (R p) {(cv p).symm b} ∧
218:       GammaPure p K M Q.phi G ∧
219:       (∀ i, f (B i) = b • eNat (rho y) v i.val) ∧
220:       (∀ i, beta i = G.symm (1 ⊗ₜ[R p] B i)) ∧
221:       ReducedBasisSpec l K M rho x y h A beta
222: def N4 (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V)
223:     (rho : L →ₗ[ℂ] Module.End ℂ V) (x y h : L) (v : V) : Prop :=
224:   ∃ Q : Residue p K, Bridge p K M Q ∧ ReducedPackage p l K M rho x y h v Q
225: 
226: def DividedLiftMatrices (l : ℤ) (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V)
227:     (a d : Module.End ℂ V) (beta : Module.Basis (I l) K (VK K M)) : Prop :=
228:   ∀ r : ℕ, ∃ xr yr : Module.End K (VK K M), Lift K M (dp a r) xr ∧ Lift K M (dp d r) yr ∧
229:     ∀ i : I l,
230:       xr (beta i) = (if r ≤ i.val then (Nat.choose (l.toNat-i.val+r) r : K) • extend l beta (i.val-r) else 0) ∧
231:       yr (beta i) = (if i.val+r ≤ l.toNat then (Nat.choose (i.val+r) r : K) • extend l beta (i.val+r) else 0)
232: def MatrixTransport (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V)
233:     (rho : L →ₗ[ℂ] Module.End ℂ V) (x y h : L) (v : V) (Q : Residue p K) : Prop :=
234:   letI := Q.phi.toAlgebra
235:   ∀ (A : Action K M rho x y h) (f : MR p M →ₗ[ℤ] V) (b : ℂ)
236:     (G : VK K M ≃ₗ[K] K ⊗[R p] MR p M)
237:     (B : Module.Basis (I l) (R p) (MR p M)) (beta : Module.Basis (I l) K (VK K M)),
238:     IotaSpec p M f → Function.Injective f → b ≠ 0 → GammaPure p K M Q.phi G →
239:     (∀ i, f (B i) = b • eNat (rho y) v i.val) →
240:     (∀ i, beta i = G.symm (1 ⊗ₜ[R p] B i)) →
241:     Matrices l A.a A.d A.t (extend l beta) ∧ DividedLiftMatrices l K M (rho x) (rho y) beta
242: def SmallPowers (l : ℤ) (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V)
243:     (rho : L →ₗ[ℂ] Module.End ℂ V) (x y h : L) : Prop :=
244:   ∀ (A : Action K M rho x y h) (r : ℕ), r ≤ l.toNat →
245:     (r.factorial : K) ≠ 0 ∧ Lift K M (dp (rho x) r) (((r.factorial : K)⁻¹) • A.a^r) ∧
246:     Lift K M (dp (rho y) r) (((r.factorial : K)⁻¹) • A.d^r)
247: def PolynomialTransport (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V)
248:     (rho : L →ₗ[ℂ] Module.End ℂ V) (x y h : L) (v : V) (Q : Residue p K) : Prop :=
249:   letI := Q.phi.toAlgebra

import Mathlib
open scoped TensorProduct
namespace LR
abbrev L := LieAlgebra.SpecialLinear.sl (Fin 2) ℂ
abbrev R (p : ℕ) := Subring.closure {q : ℚ | ∃ a b : ℤ, b ≠ 0 ∧ ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ b ∧ q = (a : ℚ) / b}
abbrev C (p : ℕ) := RestrictScalars (R p) ℚ ℂ
def cv (p : ℕ) : C p ≃+ ℂ := RestrictScalars.addEquiv (R p) ℚ ℂ
abbrev I (l : ℤ) := Fin (l.toNat + 1)
abbrev MR (p : ℕ) {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] (M : Submodule ℤ V) := (R p) ⊗[ℤ] M
abbrev VK (K : Type*) [Field K] {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] (M : Submodule ℤ V) := K ⊗[ℤ] M
noncomputable def dp {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] (f : Module.End ℂ V) (r : ℕ) : Module.End ℂ V := ((r.factorial : ℂ)⁻¹) • f ^ r

variable {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
noncomputable def eNat (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) : V := dp y i v
def Stable {F A : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup A] [Module F A] (W : Submodule F A) (f : Module.End F A) : Prop := ∀ w ∈ W, f w ∈ W
def ComplexHyp (l : ℤ) (rho : L →ₗ[ℂ] Module.End ℂ V) (x y h : L) : Prop :=
  IsSl2Triple h x y ∧ Submodule.span ℂ ({x,y,h} : Set L) = ⊤ ∧
  (∀ s t : L, rho ⁅s,t⁆ = rho s * rho t - rho t * rho s) ∧
  FiniteDimensional ℂ V ∧ Module.finrank ℂ V = l.toNat + 1 ∧
  Nontrivial V ∧
  (∀ W : Submodule ℂ V, (∀ t : L, Stable W (rho t)) → W = ⊥ ∨ W = ⊤) ∧
  (∃ w : V, w ≠ 0 ∧ rho x w = 0 ∧ rho h w = (l : ℂ) • w)
def Admissible (rho : L →ₗ[ℂ] Module.End ℂ V) (x y : L) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  (∃ (ι : Type) (b : Module.Basis ι ℤ M) (bc : Module.Basis ι ℂ V), ∀ i, (b i : V) = bc i) ∧
  (∀ r : ℕ, ∀ m ∈ M, dp (rho x) r m ∈ M ∧ dp (rho y) r m ∈ M)
def Strings (l : ℤ) (a d t : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  (∀ r : ℕ, t ((d ^ r) v) = ((l : ℂ) - 2 * (r : ℂ)) • (d ^ r) v) ∧
  (∀ r : ℕ, 0 < r → a ((d ^ r) v) = ((r : ℂ) * ((l : ℂ) - (r : ℂ) + 1)) • (d ^ (r-1)) v)
def BasisString (l : ℤ) (d : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  ∃ b : Module.Basis (I l) ℂ V, (∀ i, b i = eNat d v i.val) ∧
    (∀ r : ℕ, l.toNat < r → (d ^ r) v = 0)
def Matrices {F A : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup A] [Module F A]
    (l : ℤ) (a d t : Module.End F A) (e : ℕ → A) : Prop :=
  a (e 0) = 0 ∧
  (∀ i : ℕ, 1 ≤ i → i ≤ l.toNat → a (e i) = ((l : F) - (i : F) + 1) • e (i-1)) ∧
  (∀ i : ℕ, i < l.toNat → d (e i) = ((i : F)+1) • e (i+1)) ∧
  d (e l.toNat) = 0 ∧
  (∀ i : ℕ, i ≤ l.toNat → t (e i) = ((l : F) - 2*(i : F)) • e i)
def DividedMatrices (l : ℤ) (a d : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  ∀ r i : ℕ, i ≤ l.toNat →
    dp a r (eNat d v i) =
      (if r ≤ i then (Nat.choose (l.toNat-i+r) r : ℂ) • eNat d v (i-r) else 0) ∧
    dp d r (eNat d v i) =
      (if i+r ≤ l.toNat then (Nat.choose (i+r) r : ℂ) • eNat d v (i+r) else 0)
def N1 (l : ℤ) (a d t : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  0 < l+1 ∧ Fintype.card (I l) = (l+1).toNat ∧ Strings l a d t v ∧
  BasisString l d v ∧ Matrices l a d t (eNat d v) ∧ DividedMatrices l a d v
noncomputable def unit (l : ℤ) (b : Module.Basis (I l) ℂ V) (i j : I l) : Module.End ℂ V :=
  (b.coord j).smulRight (b i)
def BasisSpec (l : ℤ) (d : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (b : Module.Basis (I l) ℂ V) : Prop :=
  ∀ i, b i = eNat d v i.val
def LocalRingSpec (p : ℕ) : Prop :=
  (∀ q : ℚ, q ∈ R p ↔ ∃ a b : ℤ, b ≠ 0 ∧ ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ b ∧ q = (a : ℚ) / b) ∧
  (∀ b : ℤ, ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ b → IsUnit (b : R p))
def SmallUnits (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) : Prop :=
  (∀ r : ℕ, r ≤ l.toNat → ¬ p ∣ r.factorial ∧ IsUnit (r.factorial : R p)) ∧
  (∀ j : I l, IsUnit (Nat.choose l.toNat j.val : R p))
def IotaSpec (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (f : MR p M →ₗ[ℤ] V) : Prop :=
  (∀ (r : R p) (m : M), f (r ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m) = (((r : ℚ) : ℂ)) • (m : V)) ∧
  (∀ (r : R p) (z : MR p M), f (r • z) = (((r : ℚ) : ℂ)) • f z)
def LocalBasis (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (f : MR p M →ₗ[ℤ] V) : Prop :=
  Function.Injective f ∧
  Nonempty (Module.Basis (I l) (R p) (MR p M)) ∧
  Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range f) = ⊤
def Preserved (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (f : MR p M →ₗ[ℤ] V) (a d : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  (∀ r : ℕ, ∀ m ∈ M, dp a r m ∈ M ∧ dp d r m ∈ M) ∧
  (∀ r : ℕ, ∀ z : MR p M, dp a r (f z) ∈ Set.range f ∧ dp d r (f z) ∈ Set.range f)
def UnitIdentities (l : ℤ) (a d : Module.End ℂ V) (b : Module.Basis (I l) ℂ V) : Prop :=
  ∀ i j : I l,
    dp d l.toNat * dp a l.toNat = unit l b (Fin.last l.toNat) (Fin.last l.toNat) ∧
    dp a (l.toNat-i.val) * (dp d l.toNat * dp a l.toNat) = unit l b i (Fin.last l.toNat) ∧
    (dp d l.toNat * dp a l.toNat) * dp d (l.toNat-j.val) = (Nat.choose l.toNat j.val : ℂ) • unit l b (Fin.last l.toNat) j
def AllUnits (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (f : MR p M →ₗ[ℤ] V)
    (a d : Module.End ℂ V) (b : Module.Basis (I l) ℂ V) : Prop :=
  ∀ i j : I l,
    unit l b i j = ((Nat.choose l.toNat j.val : ℂ)⁻¹) •
      (dp a (l.toNat-i.val) * (dp d l.toNat * dp a l.toNat) * dp d (l.toNat-j.val)) ∧
    (∀ z : MR p M, unit l b i j (f z) ∈ Set.range f)

abbrev LZ (x y h : L) := Submodule.span ℤ ({x,y,h} : Set L)
def Lift (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) (f : Module.End ℂ V) (g : Module.End K (VK K M)) : Prop :=
  ∃ fm : Module.End ℤ M, (∀ m : M, (fm m : V) = f (m : V)) ∧
    (∀ (c : K) (m : M), g (c ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m) = c ⊗ₜ[ℤ] (fm m))
structure Action (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (rho : L →ₗ[ℂ] Module.End ℂ V) (x y h : L) where
  onM : LZ x y h →ₗ[ℤ] Module.End ℤ M
  onM_spec : ∀ s : LZ x y h, ∀ m : M, (onM s m : V) = rho (s : L) (m : V)
  bracket_mem : ∀ s t : LZ x y h, ⁅(s : L),(t : L)⁆ ∈ LZ x y h
  red : K ⊗[ℤ] LZ x y h →ₗ[K] Module.End K (VK K M)
  red_spec : ∀ (c d : K) (s : LZ x y h) (m : M),
    red (c ⊗ₜ[ℤ] s) (d ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m) = (c*d) ⊗ₜ[ℤ] onM s m
  red_lie : ∀ s t u : LZ x y h, (u : L) = ⁅(s : L),(t : L)⁆ → ∀ c d : K,
    red ((c*d) ⊗ₜ[ℤ] u) = red (c ⊗ₜ[ℤ] s) * red (d ⊗ₜ[ℤ] t) - red (d ⊗ₜ[ℤ] t) * red (c ⊗ₜ[ℤ] s)
  a : Module.End K (VK K M)
  d : Module.End K (VK K M)
  t : Module.End K (VK K M)
  a_spec : Lift K M (rho x) a
  d_spec : Lift K M (rho y) d
  t_spec : Lift K M (rho h) t
  gen_spec : ∀ (s : LZ x y h),
    ((s : L) = x → red (1 ⊗ₜ[ℤ] s) = a) ∧
    ((s : L) = y → red (1 ⊗ₜ[ℤ] s) = d) ∧
    ((s : L) = h → red (1 ⊗ₜ[ℤ] s) = t)
def N2 (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (rho : L →ₗ[ℂ] Module.End ℂ V) (x y h : L) (v : V) : Prop :=
  LocalRingSpec p ∧ SmallUnits p l ∧ Nonempty (Action K M rho x y h) ∧
  ∃ f : MR p M →ₗ[ℤ] V, IotaSpec p M f ∧ LocalBasis p l M f ∧
    Preserved p M f (rho x) (rho y) ∧
    (∀ b : Module.Basis (I l) ℂ V, BasisSpec l (rho y) v b →
      UnitIdentities l (rho x) (rho y) b ∧ AllUnits p l M f (rho x) (rho y) b)
def CoeffSpec (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (d : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (f : MR p M →ₗ[ℤ] V) (J : Submodule (R p) (C p)) : Prop :=
  (∀ (i : I l) (c : ℂ), (cv p).symm c ∈ J ↔ c • eNat d v i.val ∈ Set.range f) ∧
  J.FG ∧ J ≠ ⊥ ∧
  ∃ D : (I l → J) ≃ₗ[R p] MR p M, ∀ g : I l → J, f (D g) = ∑ i, cv p (g i : C p) • eNat d v i.val
def MuSpec (p : ℕ) (J : Submodule (R p) (C p)) (mu : ℚ ⊗[R p] J →ₗ[ℚ] ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∀ (q : ℚ) (c : J), mu (q ⊗ₜ[R p] c) = (q : ℂ) * cv p (c : C p)
def RationalEmbedding (p : ℕ) (J : Submodule (R p) (C p)) : Prop :=
  FiniteDimensional ℚ (ℚ ⊗[R p] J) ∧
  ∃ mu : ℚ ⊗[R p] J →ₗ[ℚ] ℂ, MuSpec p J mu ∧ Function.Injective mu ∧
    LinearMap.range mu = Submodule.span ℚ ((cv p) '' (J : Set (C p)))
def ScaledBasis (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (d : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (f : MR p M →ₗ[ℤ] V) (b : ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∃ B : Module.Basis (I l) (R p) (MR p M), ∀ i, f (B i) = b • eNat d v i.val
def CyclicSpec (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (d : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (f : MR p M →ₗ[ℤ] V) (J : Submodule (R p) (C p)) : Prop :=
  (∃ b : ℂ, (cv p).symm b ∈ J ∧ b ≠ 0 ∧ J = Submodule.span (R p) {(cv p).symm b}) ∧
  (∀ b : ℂ, (cv p).symm b ∈ J → b ≠ 0 → J = Submodule.span (R p) {(cv p).symm b} → ScaledBasis p l d v M f b)
def N3 (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (d : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : MR p M →ₗ[ℤ] V, IotaSpec p M f →
    ∃ J : Submodule (R p) (C p), CoeffSpec p l d v M f J ∧ RationalEmbedding p J ∧
      Module.finrank ℚ (ℚ ⊗[R p] J) = 1 ∧ CyclicSpec p l d v M f J
def RationalMultiples (p : ℕ) (J : Submodule (R p) (C p)) : Prop :=
  ∀ a : ℂ, (cv p).symm a ∈ J → a ≠ 0 → ∀ c : ℂ, (cv p).symm c ∈ J → ∃ q : ℚ, c = (q : ℂ) * a
def PDecomposition (p : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ q : ℚ, q ≠ 0 → ∃ (nu : ℤ) (u : (R p)ˣ), q = (p : ℚ)^nu * (u.val : ℚ)
def Target (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (rho : L →ₗ[ℂ] Module.End ℂ V) (x y h : L) : Prop :=
  Nontrivial (VK K M) ∧
  ∃ A : Action K M rho x y h, ∀ W : Submodule K (VK K M),
    Stable W A.a → Stable W A.d → Stable W A.t → W = ⊥ ∨ W = ⊤

structure Residue (p : ℕ) (K : Type*) [Field K] where
  phi : R p →+* K
  psi : R p →+* ZMod p
  kappa : ZMod p →+* K
  phi_fraction : ∀ (a b : ℤ) (r : R p), b ≠ 0 → ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ b →
    (r : ℚ) = (a : ℚ) / b → phi r = (a : K) * (b : K)⁻¹
  psi_fraction : ∀ (a b : ℤ) (r : R p), b ≠ 0 → ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ b →
    (r : ℚ) = (a : ℚ) / b → psi r = (a : ZMod p) * (b : ZMod p)⁻¹
  kappa_int : ∀ a : ℤ, kappa (a : ZMod p) = (a : K)
  compatible : phi = kappa.comp psi
  psi_surjective : Function.Surjective psi
  psi_kernel : RingHom.ker psi = Ideal.span {(p : R p)}
  eps : (R p) ⧸ Ideal.span {(p : R p)} ≃+* ZMod p
  eps_spec : ∀ r : R p, eps (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {(p : R p)}) r) = psi r
  units_nonzero : ∀ u : (R p)ˣ, phi u.val ≠ 0
def GammaPure (p : ℕ) (K : Type*) [Field K] [Algebra (R p) K] (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (phi : R p →+* K) (G : VK K M ≃ₗ[K] K ⊗[R p] MR p M) : Prop :=
  (∀ (c : K) (m : M), G (c ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m) = c ⊗ₜ[R p] (1 ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m)) ∧
  (∀ (c : K) (r : R p) (m : M), G.symm (c ⊗ₜ[R p] (r ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m)) = (phi r*c) ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m)
def DeltaPure (p : ℕ) (K : Type*) [Field K] [Algebra (R p) K] [Algebra (ZMod p) K]
    (M : Submodule ℤ V) (D : (K ⊗[R p] MR p M) ≃ₗ[K] (K ⊗[ZMod p] ModN (MR p M) p)) : Prop :=
  (∀ (c : K) (z : MR p M), D (c ⊗ₜ[R p] z) = c ⊗ₜ[ZMod p] ModN.mkQ p z) ∧
  (∀ (c : K) (z : MR p M), D.symm (c ⊗ₜ[ZMod p] ModN.mkQ p z) = c ⊗ₜ[R p] z)
def Bridge (p : ℕ) (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) (Q : Residue p K) : Prop :=
  letI := Q.phi.toAlgebra
  letI := Q.kappa.toAlgebra
  ∃ (G : VK K M ≃ₗ[K] K ⊗[R p] MR p M)
    (D : (K ⊗[R p] MR p M) ≃ₗ[K] (K ⊗[ZMod p] ModN (MR p M) p)),
    GammaPure p K M Q.phi G ∧ DeltaPure p K M D ∧
    (∀ (F : Module.End ℤ M) (z : VK K M),
      G (F.baseChange K z) = ((F.baseChange (R p)).baseChange K) (G z)) ∧
    (∀ F : Module.End (R p) (MR p M),
      ∃ Fb : Module.End (ZMod p) (ModN (MR p M) p),
        (∀ z : MR p M, Fb (ModN.mkQ p z) = ModN.mkQ p (F z)) ∧
        (∀ z : K ⊗[R p] MR p M, D (F.baseChange K z) = Fb.baseChange K (D z)))
noncomputable def extend {F A : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup A] [Module F A] (l : ℤ)
    (b : Module.Basis (I l) F A) (k : ℕ) : A :=
  if hk : k < l.toNat+1 then b ⟨k,hk⟩ else 0
def polynomial {F A : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup A] [Module F A]
    (l : ℤ) (a d : Module.End F A) (i j : I l) : Module.End F A :=
  (Nat.choose l.toNat j.val : F)⁻¹ •
    (((((l.toNat-i.val).factorial : F)⁻¹) • a^(l.toNat-i.val)) *
    (((l.toNat.factorial : F)⁻¹) • d^l.toNat) *
    (((l.toNat.factorial : F)⁻¹) • a^l.toNat) *
    (((((l.toNat-j.val).factorial : F)⁻¹) • d^(l.toNat-j.val))))
def ReducedBasisSpec (l : ℤ) (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (rho : L →ₗ[ℂ] Module.End ℂ V) (x y h : L) (A : Action K M rho x y h)
    (beta : Module.Basis (I l) K (VK K M)) : Prop :=
  Module.finrank K (VK K M) = l.toNat+1 ∧
  Matrices l A.a A.d A.t (extend l beta) ∧
  (∀ r : ℕ, r ≤ l.toNat →
    (r.factorial : K) ≠ 0 ∧
    Lift K M (dp (rho x) r) (((r.factorial : K)⁻¹) • A.a^r) ∧
    Lift K M (dp (rho y) r) (((r.factorial : K)⁻¹) • A.d^r)) ∧
  (∀ i j : I l, (Nat.choose l.toNat j.val : K) ≠ 0 ∧
    ∀ k : I l, polynomial l A.a A.d i j (beta k) = if k = j then beta i else 0)
def Transfer (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (d : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (Q : Residue p K) : Prop :=
  letI := Q.phi.toAlgebra
  ∀ (f : MR p M →ₗ[ℤ] V) (b : ℂ), IotaSpec p M f → ScaledBasis p l d v M f b →
    ∃ (G : VK K M ≃ₗ[K] K ⊗[R p] MR p M)
      (B : Module.Basis (I l) (R p) (MR p M)) (beta : Module.Basis (I l) K (VK K M)),
      GammaPure p K M Q.phi G ∧
      (∀ i, f (B i) = b • eNat d v i.val) ∧
      (∀ i, beta i = G.symm (1 ⊗ₜ[R p] B i)) ∧
      Module.finrank K (VK K M) = l.toNat+1
def ReducedPackage (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (rho : L →ₗ[ℂ] Module.End ℂ V) (x y h : L) (v : V) (Q : Residue p K) : Prop :=
  letI := Q.phi.toAlgebra
  ∀ A : Action K M rho x y h,
    ∃ (f : MR p M →ₗ[ℤ] V) (J : Submodule (R p) (C p)) (b : ℂ)
      (G : VK K M ≃ₗ[K] K ⊗[R p] MR p M)
      (B : Module.Basis (I l) (R p) (MR p M)) (beta : Module.Basis (I l) K (VK K M)),
      IotaSpec p M f ∧ Function.Injective f ∧ CoeffSpec p l (rho y) v M f J ∧
      (cv p).symm b ∈ J ∧ b ≠ 0 ∧ J = Submodule.span (R p) {(cv p).symm b} ∧
      GammaPure p K M Q.phi G ∧
      (∀ i, f (B i) = b • eNat (rho y) v i.val) ∧
      (∀ i, beta i = G.symm (1 ⊗ₜ[R p] B i)) ∧
      ReducedBasisSpec l K M rho x y h A beta
def N4 (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (rho : L →ₗ[ℂ] Module.End ℂ V) (x y h : L) (v : V) : Prop :=
  ∃ Q : Residue p K, Bridge p K M Q ∧ ReducedPackage p l K M rho x y h v Q

def DividedLiftMatrices (l : ℤ) (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (a d : Module.End ℂ V) (beta : Module.Basis (I l) K (VK K M)) : Prop :=
  ∀ r : ℕ, ∃ xr yr : Module.End K (VK K M), Lift K M (dp a r) xr ∧ Lift K M (dp d r) yr ∧
    ∀ i : I l,
      xr (beta i) = (if r ≤ i.val then (Nat.choose (l.toNat-i.val+r) r : K) • extend l beta (i.val-r) else 0) ∧
      yr (beta i) = (if i.val+r ≤ l.toNat then (Nat.choose (i.val+r) r : K) • extend l beta (i.val+r) else 0)
def MatrixTransport (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (rho : L →ₗ[ℂ] Module.End ℂ V) (x y h : L) (v : V) (Q : Residue p K) : Prop :=
  letI := Q.phi.toAlgebra
  ∀ (A : Action K M rho x y h) (f : MR p M →ₗ[ℤ] V) (b : ℂ)
    (G : VK K M ≃ₗ[K] K ⊗[R p] MR p M)
    (B : Module.Basis (I l) (R p) (MR p M)) (beta : Module.Basis (I l) K (VK K M)),
    IotaSpec p M f → Function.Injective f → b ≠ 0 → GammaPure p K M Q.phi G →
    (∀ i, f (B i) = b • eNat (rho y) v i.val) →
    (∀ i, beta i = G.symm (1 ⊗ₜ[R p] B i)) →
    Matrices l A.a A.d A.t (extend l beta) ∧ DividedLiftMatrices l K M (rho x) (rho y) beta
def SmallPowers (l : ℤ) (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (rho : L →ₗ[ℂ] Module.End ℂ V) (x y h : L) : Prop :=
  ∀ (A : Action K M rho x y h) (r : ℕ), r ≤ l.toNat →
    (r.factorial : K) ≠ 0 ∧ Lift K M (dp (rho x) r) (((r.factorial : K)⁻¹) • A.a^r) ∧
    Lift K M (dp (rho y) r) (((r.factorial : K)⁻¹) • A.d^r)
def PolynomialTransport (p : ℕ) (l : ℤ) (K : Type*) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (rho : L →ₗ[ℂ] Module.End ℂ V) (x y h : L) (v : V) (Q : Residue p K) : Prop :=
  letI := Q.phi.toAlgebra
  ∀ (A : Action K M rho x y h) (f : MR p M →ₗ[ℤ] V) (b : ℂ)
    (G : VK K M ≃ₗ[K] K ⊗[R p] MR p M)
    (B : Module.Basis (I l) (R p) (MR p M)) (beta : Module.Basis (I l) K (VK K M)),
    IotaSpec p M f → Function.Injective f → b ≠ 0 → GammaPure p K M Q.phi G →
    (∀ i, f (B i) = b • eNat (rho y) v i.val) →
    (∀ i, beta i = G.symm (1 ⊗ₜ[R p] B i)) →
    ∀ i j : I l, (Nat.choose l.toNat j.val : K) ≠ 0 ∧
      ∀ k : I l, polynomial l A.a A.d i j (beta k) = if k = j then beta i else 0
end LR

The traceless 2×2 complex matrix realization presents the original sl₂(ℂ); a Chevalley triple and its span state the source Chevalley-generator convention. The primitive-vector clause is the highest-weight condition relative to x,h. result.text:
1: # Audit B: endpoint fidelity and checked Lean closure
2: 
3: The stage-two policy is `endpoint-fidelity-2` (Audit B schema version 2).
4: Its semantic objects are every original external theorem E and the complete
5: final target P. P includes its parameters, quantifiers, hypotheses, domains and
6: conclusion. Accepted NL0/Audit A remains the source authority; B does not repeat
7: unchanged natural-language proof checking.
8: 
9: ## Normal final acceptance and deviation exception
10: 
11: The normal workflow uses `yui-frozen-interface-acceptance-1`. A complete independent
12: pre-proof review establishes source-to-type fidelity for every E and full P and
13: all definitions needed to interpret them. Final native inspection compares the
14: actual exported full types against that frozen contract, checks the exact defining
15: header/pins and semantic receipt, and validates standalone proof/dependency/trust
16: closure. This normal final gate is pure machine work: no additional final LLM is
17: called. It records inherited semantics, not a newly performed independent Audit B.
18: 
19: The actual E/P types include retained hypotheses and quantifiers. Text labels or
20: a source-hash check alone do not establish this gate. The original mathematical
21: review may be wrong; the machine establishes preservation of that reviewed encoding,
22: not correctness of the reviewer's natural-language judgment.
23: 
24: Only complete proof-integrity success plus genuine endpoint/definition drift may
25: open the exceptional independent B-final review below. A faithful result then has
26: `AUDIT-B-CONDITIONAL`, a freeze-deviation warning and an explicit harness-defect
27: report. Invalid native evidence, incomplete dependencies or changed provenance
28: cannot be overridden semantically. Nonfaithful/unverified results wait for the
29: three explicit user choices in [proof repair](proof-repair.md); accepting a different
30: result does not complete the original target. Explicit/manual legacy semantic
31: receipts remain supported under their original schemas and are not relabeled.
32: Explicitly nonindependent/self-review records remain readable development checks;
33: they cannot grant whole-workflow Audit B acceptance. The same qualification rule
34: applies to supplied Audit A authority and incremental producer/cut reviews.
35: 
36: ## Author correspondence explanations
37: 
38: During interface authoring, provide `endpoint_correspondence`, keyed by every
39: E ID and P. Each entry is `{mode: direct|equivalent, explanation: string}`.
40: Keep it short and useful; do not restate the entire proof or manufacture a
41: line-by-line formalization commentary:
42: 
43: - **Direct:** identify the corresponding variables, hypotheses and assertion.
44:   One sentence is enough when the translation is immediate.
45: - **Equivalent:** explain the mathematical identification or reformulation,
46:   why it works in both directions and which existing conditions it uses.
47:   Point to relevant definitions or checked conversions when needed.
48: 
49: For example, expressing invariance under a finite basis of operators can encode
50: invariance under their linear span: explain the spanning property and closure
51: of a subspace under linear combinations. The review must establish those facts
52: for the actual source algebra/action; the word “equivalent” alone is insufficient.
53: 
54: The postprocessing author carries these notes into each E/P entry in
55: `mapping.json`, checks them against the actual export and completes missing
56: notes for older frozen contracts. It must not change frozen proof statements
57: or bodies merely to improve a note. An explanation is an author's claim, not
58: an Audit B verdict or a formal proof.
59: 
60: ## Semantic responsibility before freeze or at explicit B-final
61: 
62: Read the explanation together with the original source statement and actual
63: elaborated Lean type. Follow the definitions needed to interpret the endpoint,
64: including structure fields that might hide extra assumptions. Check each E/P
65: row, then these four global checks:
66: 
67: 1. `endpoint_inventory_and_scope`: all original E statements and P are covered;
68:    the source version, reviewer scope and inherited qualifications are explicit.
69: 2. `external_statement_fidelity`: each external assumption has the source's
70:    complete mathematical meaning, including conditions and quantifiers. With
71:    no external inputs, record that fact.
72: 3. `complete_target_and_representations`: the entire target theorem has the
73:    same meaning, including every hypothesis. Validate the explanation of each
74:    direct or equivalent encoding and relevant edge cases.
75: 4. `kernel_closure_and_trust`: the actual exported proof compiled, all required
76:    producers and intermediate library ports were discharged, and the checked
77:    root has only the declared external assumptions and permitted foundations.
78: 
79: Equivalent formulations are allowed. Do not reject a faithful encoding because
80: it lacks a particular Mathlib type/name, a separate object for every NL0
81: D node, or a duplicate formal representation. A mathematical source-to-code
82: identification can be checked semantically without constructing an unnecessary
83: second model. If the implementation actually crosses two different Lean
84: representations, the required conversion must occur in checked Lean code.
85: Unexplained equivalence, stronger assumptions, missing hypotheses, changed
86: domains or hidden target assumptions remain defects.
87: 
88: Do not accept an explanation on trust or copy the author's conclusion into the
89: review. Record PASS/FAIL/UNVERIFIED with specific findings and source/type/note
90: locations. A compiler pass cannot substitute for this independent judgment.
91: 
92: ## Freely available Mathlib
93: 
94: All proved results in the pinned Mathlib environment are available in stage
95: two. Do not compare their names, counts or node-by-node uses with the NL0 M
96: inventory. There is no per-M semantic row, imported-proof whitelist,
97: `calculation_links` ledger, or separate review of implementation N/D nodes.
98: Definitions are examined when they determine endpoint meaning, not for an
99: exact inventory match. Notes from Audit A are optional local guidance, not
100: permissions to use a library theorem.
101: 
102: New interfaces normally use Mathlib directly. An older or deliberately
103: conditional interface can retain M ports; `library_terms` supplies an actual
104: Lean proof for each such port at assembly. These are discharge proofs, not a
105: library correspondence inventory. They cannot remain unproved assumptions of
106: the final export. New external axioms or stronger project hypotheses still
107: require returning to the affected source boundary.
108: 
109: ## Mechanical evidence and limits
110: 
111: ### Compact review materials
112: 
113: The semantic reviewer reads the separately versioned
114: `yui-audit-b-review-view-1` in `review-packet.json`. Start at `/scope` and
115: `/mechanical_summary`, then examine each `/endpoints/<ID>` source, actual
116: inspected type and author correspondence. P retains the complete original
117: target, parameters and hypotheses. The view is a deterministic Python extraction,
118: not an LLM summary or mathematical judgment. It never substitutes a declared
119: expected type for the actual inspected type.
120: 
121: `/documents` identifies hash-bound `source-context.json`, `source-original.txt`
122: and actual `Proof.lean`. Read relevant original and Lean definitions there,
123: including hidden structure fields, when needed to interpret an endpoint.
124: Complete raw compiler, elaboration and dependency records stay in the machine
125: archive; they are not default reviewer inputs. A mechanical summary reports
126: actual checks and exceptions, without populating a semantic PASS. The full
127: dependency inspection remains a program responsibility.
128: 
129: Use `read_task_input` JSON pointers, not guessed fixed line positions. Large
130: containers expose keys and large strings expose `next_offset`. Text reads
131: resume with `next_start` and `next_column`. Serialized read results are at most
132: 32 KiB; follow `has_more` until the needed statement is complete. This pagination
133: limit is not a task time/token/call budget. Unknown calls or modified feedback
134: remain rejected with a specific local protocol fault, not a retryable HTTP 502.
135: 
136: ### Explicit reuse of completed native evidence
137: 
138: `audit_b.py reuse-review <new-directory> --original <old-audit-directory>`
139: prepares a new semantic review without rebuilding or changing Lean. It validates
140: every original input and snapshot, the original native artifacts/output, source
141: and accepted-A authority, environment pins, and the exact historical tool
142: snapshots. The new view and current reviewer runtime are separately bound in
143: `review-reuse.json`; the normal current-build tool check is not disabled.
144: Changed or incomplete evidence blocks reuse. Preserve the original failure.
145: 
146: The new independent reviewer receives no previous B verdict, reviewer history,
147: owner reasoning or other-case material. The receipt discloses inherited native
148: checks and a new semantic review; it cannot claim fresh compilation, an unaided
149: cold whole-workflow success or measured acceleration. Changing proofs or source
150: requires the appropriate new checks, rather than this review-only path.
151: 
152: `audit_b.py prepare/build/check` binds the source, accepted A, contract, plan,
153: proofs, tool versions and environment hashes. Build compiles standalone
154: `Proof.lean` before adding inspection. It checks E/P against their declared
155: encoded types, modulo definitional equality and bijective universe renaming.
156: It does not prove equivalence between natural-language text and Lean.
157: Distinct universes must not be collapsed; changed types or hypotheses must not
158: be normalized away. Source fidelity is established by the bound pre-proof independent review, or an actual exceptional B-final review; this native comparison does not establish it anew.
159: 
160: Inspection follows the actual `AuditBExport.P` closure. No `sorry`, unproved
161: local axiom/opaque substitute or undeclared foundation may be introduced.
162: Local bodies still compile against their own task inputs and the pinned
163: library; every required producer must exist. Assembly, inspection and semantic
164: review have separate recorded outcomes.
165: 
166: Version-1 receipts remain historical results under their original policy.
167: They cannot be silently relabeled or accepted as version-2 reviews. Start a
168: new bound audit when policy, source, code or evidence changes. Pending templates
169: never pass. A whole accepted source plus complete native gates and its bound semantic
170: authority yields `AUDIT-B-PASSED`; a fragment yields at most the explicitly
171: scoped development verdict. A whole source with an actual conditional Audit A
172: can yield `AUDIT-B-CONDITIONAL` after all the same native and semantic checks.
173: It retains the exact source warnings and never upgrades them to full PASS.
174: Neither proves external publications in Lean or
175: establishes formalizer speedup. Preserve failures and report actual costs.

value.text: H001 gives λ≥0, so n=λ+1>0 and I consists of exactly n integers. We prove the string identities simultaneously by natural induction on t≥0. At t=0, hv=λv and xv=0 are H003. In the induction step temporarily assume L1: h y^t v=(λ−2t)y^t v and, when t≥1, x y^t v=t(λ−t+1)y^(t−1)v (with xv=0 at t=0). The relation hy=yh−2y from H002 gives h y^(t+1)v=(λ−2t−2)y^(t+1)v. The relation xy=yx+h gives x y^(t+1)v=y(x y^t v)+h y^t v=[t(λ−t+1)+λ−2t]y^t v=(t+1)(λ−t)y^t v, also at t=0 using xv=0. This proves the step and discharges L1; natural induction gives both identities for all t in their stated ranges.

For each i∈I, repeated application of the x identity in F001 gives x^i y^i v=i!λ(λ−1)⋯(λ−i+1)v. At i=0 the product is empty and equals 1; at i≥1 its factors are positive integers, since i≤λ. Since v≠0 by H003, this shows e_i≠0 over ℂ. F001 gives h e_i=(λ−2i)e_i. To prove independence, fix coefficients c and temporarily assume L2: Σ_(i∈I)c_i e_i=0. Fix j∈I and apply ∏_(k∈I,k≠j)(h−(λ−2k)Id_V). Every term except j is zero; the j term is c_j [∏_(k≠j)2(k−j)]e_j. All its factors are nonzero complex numbers and e_j≠0, so c_j=0. Since j was arbitrary, all coefficients vanish. Discharging L2 proves independence.

Apply M001 to the division ring ℂ, the complex vector space V, the finite index set I and the family e. F002 supplies independence, F001 gives |I|=n, and H002 gives dim_ℂ V=λ+1=n and finite dimensionality. Thus the span of e is V, so together with independence it is a basis. By F001, y^(λ+1)v has eigenvalue −λ−2 under h. Expand this vector in the basis e; comparison of each coefficient in h y^(λ+1)v=(−λ−2)y^(λ+1)v gives [λ−2i−(−λ−2)] times that coefficient zero. For i∈I this multiplier is 2(λ+1−i)≠0 in ℂ. Every coefficient is zero, hence y^(λ+1)v=0. Applying further powers of y gives all higher vanishing.

For arbitrary i∈I divide the identities F001 by i!: x e_0=0, and for i≥1, x e_i=(λ−i+1)e_(i−1). Directly y e_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for i<λ, while y e_λ=0 by F003. Also h e_i=(λ−2i)e_i. These are the required integer action matrices.

Fix r≥0. Iterating the x matrix in F004 and dividing by r! gives X(r)e_i=[(λ−i+1)⋯(λ−i+r)/r!]e_(i−r)=binom(λ−i+r,r)e_(i−r) when r≤i. When r>i, iteration reaches x e_0=0 and gives zero. Similarly iteration of y gives Y(r)e_i=[(i+1)⋯(i+r)/r!]e_(i+r)=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) if i+r≤λ, and gives zero past the terminating string. These binomial coefficients have nonnegative top at least r. They are integers: for every nonnegative integer a₀, the factorial expressions have boundary values binom(a₀,0)=binom(a₀,a₀)=1 and satisfy binom(a₀,s)=binom(a₀−1,s−1)+binom(a₀−1,s) for 0<s<a₀ by a common-denominator calculation. Induction on a₀, proving the assertion simultaneously for all 0≤s≤a₀, proves integrality. This establishes every divided-power formula in the exported conclusion as well as its zero cases.

Since p is prime by H001, p≥2 and the integers not divisible by p are multiplicatively closed. Fraction addition and multiplication therefore make R a subring of ℚ⊂ℂ; in particular every integer b with p∤b is a unit, with inverse 1/b∈R. By H004 choose a simultaneous integer basis B of M and complex basis B of V. It has finitely many vectors since V has finite dimension n by H002. M010 applied to the nontrivial commutative ring ℂ supplies its strong rank condition. M003 applied to its complex basis gives that its number of vectors is dim_ℂ V=n. By N001, |I|=n; reindexing the basis by I yields the existence stated in F001.

Choose m as in F001. Apply M002 with R₀=ℤ, A=M, S₀=R and the integer basis m. It gives the R-basis (1⊗m_i)_(i∈I) of M_R. The map ι_M sends these basis vectors to m_i; a finite R-linear relation among their images is also a complex-linear relation, so all coefficients are zero. Thus ι_M is injective, identifies M_R with the R-span of the m_i inside V, and its complex span is V. For any r≥0, admissibility H004 and D005 imply X(r)M⊂M and Y(r)M⊂M; R-linearity gives preservation of M_R. In particular X(1)=x and Y(1)=y preserve M; H002 gives h=xy−yx on V, so h preserves M as well. The commutators in H002 show directly that the integer span of x,y,h is bracket-closed, since all three structure constants are integers. For arbitrary t₀∈ℤx+ℤy+ℤh and z_M∈M the restriction t₀z_M is in M. The rule (t₀⊗c₀)(z_M⊗d₀)=t₀z_M⊗(c₀d₀), for arbitrary c₀,d₀∈K, respects addition and both integer balancing relations, hence defines a K-bilinear action on the two tensor products. Its Lie representation identity is verified on pure tensors by the identity in the given complex Lie module V, and then on finite sums by bilinearity. Thus it is the asserted induced Lie action, without identifying the Chevalley integer form with any different reduction.

For every integer 0≤r≤λ, apply M006 with ℓ=p and u=r. H001 supplies primality and r≤λ<p, so p∤r!. Thus r! is a unit of R. In particular λ!, j!, (λ−j)! are all units, for j∈I. Their ratio binom(λ,j)=λ!/[j!(λ−j)!] is a unit of R, with inverse j!(λ−j)!/λ!. The factorials are positive and therefore nonzero as rational numbers. These statements also cover r=0.

We now identify operators by their actions on the complex basis e from N001. In Y(λ)X(λ), every basis vector below e_λ is killed by X(λ); on e_λ, X(λ)e_λ=e_0 and Y(λ)e_0=e_λ. Hence Π=E_λλ. Next X(λ−i)e_λ=e_i, with coefficient binom(λ−λ+λ−i,λ−i)=1, giving X(λ−i)Π=E_iλ. For ΠY(λ−j), an input e_k with k<j is carried below e_λ and killed by Π; if k>j the lowering string terminates and gives zero; on e_j its coefficient is binom(λ,λ−j)=binom(λ,j) and its image is e_λ. Therefore ΠY(λ−j)=binom(λ,j)E_λj. All statements include λ=0, when every factor is the identity on the one-dimensional space.

Combining F004, or applying it to each e_k, gives X(λ−i)ΠY(λ−j)=binom(λ,j)E_ij. Invert the coefficient using F003 to get E_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1)X(λ−i)ΠY(λ−j). Every factor on the right preserves M_R by F002 and R-linearity, hence every E_ij preserves M_R. With F002 and F003 this proves the entire exported conclusion.

Use the embedding from N002 throughout to regard M_R as a submodule of V. By N001 its vectors have unique coordinates in e. Since E_ii preserves M_R by N002, the ith coordinate projection maps M_R onto J_i e_i. For arbitrary i,j₁∈I and c₁∈J_(j₁), E(i,j₁)(c₁ e_(j₁))=c₁ e_i∈M_R, giving J_(j₁)⊂J_i; the reverse inclusion follows by exchanging the two coordinate indices. Thus all J_i equal J. Choose the R-basis m of M_R supplied by N002. The finitely many ith coordinates of m generate J_i, since each vector of M_R is a finite R-linear combination of m, and conversely these coordinates lie in J_i by E_ii-stability. Hence J is finitely generated. It is nonzero: temporarily assume L1: J={0}. Then every coordinate projection of M_R would vanish, so M_R would be zero, contradicting its complex span V and the nonzero basis vector e_0 in N001. This contradiction discharges L1 and proves J≠{0}. Finally the maps M_R→J^I taking coordinates, and (c_i)↦Σ c_i e_i, are mutually inverse R-linear maps. The latter sum is in M_R since each c_i e_i is; independence in N001 gives uniqueness. This proves the direct sum decomposition without any rank assumption on a submodule of ℂ.

Define U and μ as declared, and choose a nonempty finite list g of nonzero R-generators of J from F001; let k≥1 be its length, and write it g_1,...,g_k. For any rational q₀ and any finite R-linear combination Σ_(j=1)^k r_j g_j, tensor bilinearity gives q₀⊗Σ r_j g_j=Σ(q₀r_j)(1⊗g_j). Consequently the finite set {1⊗g_j:1≤j≤k} spans U over ℚ. Apply M008 with F=ℚ and A=U to this finite set; since the span is all of U, U is finite-dimensional. To check injectivity of μ, let s₀≥0 be arbitrary, take arbitrary families Q_1,...,Q_(s₀)∈ℚ and C_1,...,C_(s₀)∈J, and set z₀=Σ_(l=1)^(s₀)Q_l⊗C_l. Every element of the algebraic tensor product has such a finite-sum presentation. Define D to be the product of the positive denominators of the Q_l (the empty product is 1), and put H_l=D Q_l∈ℤ. Then D is a nonzero integer and tensor balancing over R, which contains ℤ, gives z₀=(1/D)⊗Σ H_l C_l. Temporarily assume L2: μ(z₀)=0. Its image is (1/D)Σ H_l C_l, so Σ H_l C_l=0 in ℂ, hence z₀=0 in U. Discharge L2. Since the finite presentation was arbitrary, the kernel of μ is zero, which proves injectivity by applying this to the difference of any two tensors with equal images. Its image is exactly span_ℚ J, since it consists of finite rational combinations of elements of J and contains them all.

Define T=ℚ⊗_R M_R. The inclusion R⊂ℚ gives a commutative R-algebra structure on ℚ. Apply M002 to the R-basis m: the n vectors 1⊗m_i form a ℚ-basis of T. M010 applies to the nontrivial commutative ring ℚ. M003 with this basis gives dim_ℚ T=n, since |I|=n by N001.

Define Θ:T→U^I by Θ(q₀⊗Σ c_i e_i)=(q₀⊗c_i)_i, and define Ψ in the reverse direction by summing the maps q₀⊗c↦q₀⊗(c e_i) on coordinates. The coordinate maps in F001 are R-linear, so these balanced maps extend to ℚ-linear maps of the indicated tensor products. The composites ΘΨ and ΨΘ are identities: on an elementary tensor in a single coordinate the first is that same coordinate tensor, and on q₀⊗z the second is q₀⊗Σ c_i e_i=q₀⊗z. Additivity and generation by pure tensors prove the identities everywhere. Therefore Θ is a linear equivalence. Set r_J=dim_ℚ U. By F002, U is finitely generated over ℚ, and M009 says it is free. With M010 supplying the strong rank condition for ℚ, apply M004 to the finite constant family U indexed by I; it gives dim_ℚ(U^I)=Σ_(i∈I)r_J=n r_J. Apply M005 to Θ and combine with F003 to obtain n=n r_J. Since n>0 by N001, integer arithmetic yields r_J=1.

Choose a nonzero a∈J from F001. Then 1⊗a is nonzero in U, since μ(1⊗a)=a≠0. The singleton family consisting of 1⊗a is linearly independent: multiplying a putative scalar relation by μ gives that scalar times a zero in ℂ. Apply M001 over ℚ to this singleton and U, whose finite dimension is one by F002 and F004. It spans U. Consequently every 1⊗g_j is q_j(1⊗a) for some rational q_j; apply μ to get g_j=q_j a. As every g_j≠0, each q_j≠0. This proves existence of the full finite rational family needed next.

Choose q from F005, and fix 1≤j≤k. Write q_j=A/B with its nonzero integer numerator A and positive integer denominator B. By H001, p≥2, so p≠1. Apply M007 first to |A|≠0, then to B≠0, with ℓ=p. Choose d_N,u_N,d_D,u_D as in those applications, so |A|=p^d_N u_N, B=p^d_D u_D and neither u_N nor u_D is divisible by p. They are nonzero because A,B are. Hence q_j=p^(d_N−d_D)((A/|A|)u_N/u_D). Since A/|A| is either 1 or −1, the rational (A/|A|)u_N/u_D and its inverse belong to R by the defining denominator condition, so this factor is a unit. This proves, for every j in the finite list, the claimed decomposition into an integral power of p and a unit of R, and therefore the existence of simultaneous finite families in F006.

Choose ν_j,u_j from F006 and let ν be the minimum of the finite nonempty integer list ν_1,...,ν_k; choose j₀ attaining it. Such a minimum exists by repeatedly taking the smaller of two integers. Put b=p^ν a. This is nonzero, since p≠0 and a≠0. For each j, g_j=p^(ν_j−ν)u_j b lies in Rb because ν_j−ν≥0. Conversely g_(j₀)=u_(j₀)b, so b=u_(j₀)^(-1)g_(j₀) belongs to J. Thus the R-module generated by the g_j is exactly Rb, and J=Rb. Under F001, every vector of M_R is a sum Σ r_i b e_i, while any relation Σ r_i b e_i=0 has all r_i b=0 by the complex independence of e in N001, and hence all r_i=0. Thus (b e_i) is an R-basis. The same spanning and independence argument works for any nonzero b with J=Rb. Together with F001, F002 and F004 this proves the exported conclusion.

By H001, an integer maps to zero in K exactly when divisible by p. Thus for arbitrary integers A₀,B₀ with B₀≠0 and p∤B₀, the fraction A₀/B₀∈R has a nonzero denominator image in K; and φ(A₀/B₀)=(A₀·1_K)(B₀·1_K)^(-1) is defined. Equality of fractions follows by cross multiplication, so the formula is well-defined and preserves addition, multiplication and 1. The same formula in F_p gives ψ:R→F_p. It is onto, since every integer residue occurs, and its kernel is pR: ψ(A₀/B₀)=0 is equivalent to p∣A₀, hence A₀/B₀=p((A₀/p)/B₀). Conversely multiples of p have zero image. The induced map R/pR→F_p is therefore a bijective ring map. Both constructions agree with the usual inclusion F_p→K. Every unit of R has nonzero image in K, since its image has a multiplicative inverse. In particular N002 shows that r! for 0≤r≤λ and binom(λ,j), j∈I, have nonzero images in K.

Define Γ and Γ' by Γ(m⊗c)=(1⊗m)⊗c and Γ'((r⊗m)⊗c)=m⊗φ(r)c. The defining ℤ-balancing relations in R⊗_ℤ M and in M⊗_ℤ K, and the R-balancing relation in M_R⊗_R K, show that these formulas extend to K-linear maps. They are inverse: Γ'Γ(m⊗c)=m⊗c, and ΓΓ'((r⊗m)⊗c)=(1⊗m)⊗φ(r)c=(r⊗m)⊗c. These tensors generate, so the composites are identities. Next define Δ(z⊗c)=[z]⊗c and Δ'([z]⊗c)=z⊗c. Because p acts as zero on K, changing the lift z by pz' changes the second formula by pz'⊗c=z'⊗pc=0. Using F001, scalar balancing in F_p=R/pR gives the remaining balancing condition; thus both maps are well-defined and K-linear. Their composites are identities on pure tensors. This proves the two scalar-extension isomorphisms with exactly the formulas in the exported conclusion. An operator preserving M extends on all these tensors by applying it to the lattice factor; the displayed formulas commute with that operation. For Δ this also holds for any R-linear operator of M_R, since it preserves pM_R.

Choose b≠0 with J=Rb from N003. That input proves that (b e_i)_(i∈I), regarded in M_R via the injective map ι_M of N002, is an R-basis. Apply M002 with R₀=R, S₀=K and this basis, using φ from F001. It yields the K-basis (1⊗b e_i) of K⊗_R M_R. The tensor flip z⊗c↦c⊗z is K-linear, well-defined by balancing, and inverse to the reverse flip. Therefore (b e_i⊗1) is a basis of M_R⊗_R K. Transporting it by Γ^(-1) gives the K-basis β_i defined above: inverse linear maps carry spanning families to spanning families and relations to the same relations. Apply M010 to the nontrivial commutative field K, then M003 to β to obtain dim_K V_K=|I|=n>0 using N001.

Put a=ρ_K(x⊗1), d=ρ_K(y⊗1), t=ρ_K(h⊗1). By N001, complex linearity gives x(b e_i)=b x e_i, y(b e_i)=b y e_i, and h(b e_i)=b h e_i. N002 guarantees all these lattice operations are defined, and F002 transports their tensors. Thus aβ_0=0; aβ_i=(λ−i+1)β_(i−1) for i≥1; dβ_i=(i+1)β_(i+1) for i<λ, dβ_λ=0; tβ_i=(λ−2i)β_i. The coefficients are the images of the same integers in K. The identical reasoning using N001 for X(r),Y(r) gives their integral divided-power matrices on this basis for all r≥0, including the stated zero cases. Likewise each E_ij preserves M_R by N002 and acts there by E_ij(b e_k)=b e_i if k=j and equals zero otherwise, so its scalar extension, transported by Γ^(-1), is the coordinate matrix unit of β.

Fix 0≤r≤λ. As operators on M, the characteristic-zero definitions give r!X(r)=x^r and r!Y(r)=y^r; N002 gives their preservation of M. Tensoring these equalities gives the same equalities of induced operators on V_K. By F001, r!≠0 in K, so the induced divided powers equal (r!)^(-1)a^r and (r!)^(-1)d^r. The equality E_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1)X(λ−i)Y(λ)X(λ)Y(λ−j) in N002 is an equality of R-linear operators on M_R. Extending scalars and transporting by Γ^(-1) preserves sums and compositions: this follows directly by evaluating on each pure tensor z⊗c. Substitute the divided-power equalities, whose indices λ−i, λ, λ−j all lie between 0 and λ. The result is T_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1)((λ−i)!)^(-1)a^(λ−i) (λ!)^(-1)d^λ (λ!)^(-1)a^λ ((λ−j)!)^(-1)d^(λ−j), with rightmost factor applied first. Every scalar inverse exists by F001. F004 gives T_ij β_k=β_i if k=j and zero otherwise. Along with F001–F004 this proves every assertion of the exported conclusion, including the two natural tensor identifications and positive dimension.

N002 proves x,y,h preserve M and their integer span is a Lie algebra, which supplies the construction guard for ρ_K. Choose β from N004; set a,d,T as declared. N004 states that every scalar inverse in the polynomial T exists and T_ijβ_k equals β_i when k=j and zero otherwise. Fix any K-linear subspace W⊂V_K and temporarily assume L1: W is invariant under ρ_K(x⊗1), ρ_K(y⊗1), and ρ_K(h⊗1). Thus a and d preserve W. Repeated composition shows by finite induction that every nonnegative power of either preserves W; the identity also preserves W. Composing these powers and multiplying by K-scalars preserves W by the subspace axioms. Every polynomial T_ij in N004 therefore preserves W.

First temporarily assume L3: W={0}. Then the disjunction W={0} or W=V_K follows immediately; discharge L3, giving F002. For the other branch temporarily assume L2: W≠{0}. By this inequality and the subspace zero axiom, some nonzero vector lies in W. Expanding it in the basis β gives coefficients in K. If all coefficients were zero the vector would be zero, so at least one coefficient is nonzero. This establishes the simultaneous witnesses in F003 before choosing them.

Under L2 choose w,c,j from F003. For any i∈I, F001 and K-linearity give T_ij w=Σ_(k∈I)c_k T_ijβ_k=c_jβ_i∈W. Since c_j≠0 in the field K, multiplication by c_j^(-1) gives β_i∈W. As i was arbitrary, every vector in the basis β lies in W, so W=V_K. Discharge L2 to obtain F004.

The alternatives W={0} and W≠{0} exhaust all cases. F002 and F004 therefore yield W={0} or W=V_K. Discharge L1 and universally quantify the arbitrary W to obtain the required assertion for every invariant K-subspace. N001 gives n=λ+1>0 and N004 gives a K-basis of V_K of that cardinality, so V_K is nonzero. The three generators span L_K, so their invariant subspaces are exactly L_K-submodules by K-linearity of ρ_K. H001 includes λ=0 and p=2: at λ=0 all powers and factorials used in T are zeroth powers and 1; if p=2 then λ is 0 or 1, and all preceding invertibilities still hold. No distinctness of h-eigenvalues in K was used; distinctness was used only over ℂ in N001. K was used solely as a field of characteristic p, so it need not be algebraically closed. This proves the full exported target.

value.statement: p is prime, K has characteristic p, and λ is an integer with 0≤λ<p.

V=V(λ) is the complex irreducible highest-weight sl₂(ℂ)-module of highest weight λ, has complex dimension λ+1, and its Chevalley generators x,y,h satisfy [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=−2y, [x,y]=h, both in sl₂(ℂ) and in their actions on V.
v∈V is nonzero, xv=0 and hv=λv.

M⊂V is an admissible lattice: it is a free abelian subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis of V, and it is stable under U_Z. The lattice is arbitrary; it is not assumed to be the minimal lattice.

n=λ+1>0 and |I|=n. The vectors (e_i)_(i∈I) form a complex basis of V. For every integer t≥0, h y^t v=(λ−2t)y^t v, and for t≥1, x y^t v=t(λ−t+1)y^(t−1)v. Moreover y^(λ+1)v=0 and all higher powers on v vanish. Their action matrices are x e_0=0, x e_i=(λ−i+1)e_(i−1) for 1≤i≤λ; y e_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for 0≤i<λ, y e_λ=0; h e_i=(λ−2i)e_i for i∈I. For every integer r≥0 and i∈I, X(r)e_i=binom(λ−i+r,r)e_(i−r) if r≤i and zero otherwise; Y(r)e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) if i+r≤λ and zero otherwise. Each displayed nonzero coefficient is an integer. Here binom(a,r)=a!/(r!(a−r)!) for integers 0≤r≤a; these are the usual integer binomial coefficients.

R is the subring ℤ_(p) of ℚ⊂ℂ. The map ι_M:R⊗_ℤ M→V is injective. With M_R identified with its image it is a free R-module with an R-basis of n elements and its complex span is V. Each X(r),Y(r), r≥0, preserves M and M_R. The operators x,y,h preserve M; ℤx+ℤy+ℤh is closed under the Lie bracket. For t∈ℤx+ℤy+ℤh, m∈M and c,d∈K, the rule (t⊗c)(m⊗d)=tm⊗(cd) is well-defined on (ℤx+ℤy+ℤh)⊗_ℤ K and V_K=M⊗_ℤ K and defines a K-linear Lie action. For every integer 0≤r≤λ, p∤r!, so r! is a unit in R. For all i,j∈I, binom(λ,j) is a unit in R and Π=E_λλ, X(λ−i)Π=E_iλ, ΠY(λ−j)=binom(λ,j)E_λj, and E_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1)X(λ−i)ΠY(λ−j). Consequently all E_ij preserve M_R.
